newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan central bank CD auction yields fall.
newsitem.headline: Jordan central bank CD auction yields fall.

text.p: The Central Bank of Jordan on Thursday said yields dropped at its latest auction of 140 million dinars ($197.5 million) worth of bi-monthly certificates of deposit (CDs).

The average yield for three-month paper announced for the competitive auction which closed on Wednesday fell to 8.124 percent from 8.39 at the last auction. Six-month paper also dropped to 8.20 percent from 8.46.
The yield offers for three-month paper which were accepted were in a 8.90-7.75 percent range, compared to a 8.50-8.00 percent range in the last auction.
Six-month CD yield offers which were accepted by the bank were in a 8.25-8.00 percent range against a 8.55-8.25 percent range in the previous auction.
Total bids received were 191.7 million dinars, of which 68.1 million were for three-month paper and the remaining 123.6 million bids offered for six-month paper.
The three-month paper was covered 0.97 times, while the six-month paper was covered 1.77 times.
The Central Bank sold 68.1 million dinars worth of three-month CDs and 70 million dinars of six-month CDs.

Last month the bank for the first time introduced a market-dictated CD auction system and began announcing yields in line with supply and demand as part of moves to adopt a move flexible interest rate structure.
Previously interest rates on three-month paper had been fixed for more than a year at 9.25 percent and for six-month paper at 9.50 percent.

The Central Bank maintains a monetary policy which preserves a minimum three percent differential between the local currency and dollar to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.
